mainTopic: Palm and cedar as images of the צדיק; stories and rules about fasting for rain, the deep waters, and when a rain fast ends
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why the פסוק compares a צדיק to both a palm tree and a cedar: the palm gives fruit, and the cedar regrows. A ברייתא seems to say cedars do not regrow, and the גמרא answers that there are ten kinds of cedar. Next come stories of fasting for rain. רבי אליעזר's people cry and rain falls. Later רבי עקיבא's short prayer is answered because he is forgiving. A ברייתא then gives how deep the rain must soak before a fast may end, and teaches that water from the deep rises to meet the rain. The deep calls to the deep when water is poured on the altar on סוכות, and the angel רידיא commands the waters. The גמרא then discusses when rain during a fast lets people stop fasting, and רבי אמי rules like רבי יהודה's midday cutoff. שמואל הקטן teaches that rain coming too early or too late does not prove merit; only an answer at the very moment of prayer does. Finally, the גמרא asks why the people of לוד ate before saying הלל, and אביי and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the verse also says 'cedar'
steps.stepSummary: A palm tree does not regrow after being cut down. So the פסוק adds 'cedar' to show that a צדיק does recover.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Just as a palm tree] does not regrow from its stump, so too a צדיק, Heaven forbid, would not recover. That is why the פסוק says 'cedar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a thought it started just before this point. If the פסוק had only said 'palm tree,' we would wrongly think a צדיק cannot bounce back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A palm tree does not grow new shoots once it is cut down. If the צדיק were compared only to a palm, we might think that when he is knocked down, he stays down. Adding 'cedar,' a tree that does regrow, teaches that a צדיק recovers.
steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of a sentence. The words just before it are 'Had it said palm tree and not cedar, I would say: just as a palm tree...'

phrases.english: its trunk does not grow back,
so too a righteous person, Heaven forbid,
his trunk would not grow back —
phrases.notes: He means the צדיק would never recover after something bad happens to him.

phrases.english: therefore it says 'cedar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first half of a two-part explanation that started before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'cedar' teaches that a צדיק regrows and recovers, unlike a palm tree.

steps.title: Why the verse also says 'palm tree'
steps.stepSummary: A cedar gives no fruit. So the פסוק adds 'palm tree' to show that a צדיק does produce fruit, meaning reward. That is why both trees are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had said only 'cedar,' I would have said: just as a cedar gives no fruit, so too a צדיק, Heaven forbid, gives no fruit. That is why it says both 'palm tree' and 'cedar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the explanation. The cedar alone would also give a wrong picture, so both trees are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each tree has a strength and a weakness. The palm gives fruit but does not regrow, and the cedar regrows but gives no fruit. Naming both teaches that a צדיק gets both good things: he recovers and he bears fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: The two trees fill in each other's weak spot. The palm teaches that a צדיק gives fruit, and the cedar teaches that a צדיק regrows.

phrases.english: Had it said 'cedar'
and not said 'palm tree,'
I would have said:
just as a cedar does not produce fruit,

phrases.aramaic: אַף צַדִּיק חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֵין עוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת —
phrases.english: so too a righteous person, Heaven forbid, does not produce fruit —
therefore it says 'palm tree' and it says 'cedar.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror image of step 1 and finishes the explanation of why both trees are named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'palm tree' teaches that a צדיק bears fruit, so the פסוק needs both trees.

steps.title: Challenge: a teaching says cedars do not regrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a cedar can regrow when a ברייתא about buying trees for wood says cedars do not grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a cedar really regrow? But a ברייתא teaches: someone who buys a tree from his friend to cut down must cut one טפח above the ground. For a big sycamore, he leaves two טפחים. For a sycamore that was never cut, he leaves three. For reeds and vines, he cuts from the knot and up. For palms and cedars, he may dig down and pull out the roots, because their trunk does not grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 1, which said a cedar regrows. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a buyer who may take only the wood, while the tree stays the seller's. So the buyer must leave enough stump for the tree to regrow. For palms and cedars he may pull out everything, because they will not regrow anyway. That clashes with the idea that the cedar in the פסוק regrows.

keyTerms.meaning: but was it not taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: And does a cedar's trunk grow back?
But was it not taught:
One who buys a tree from his friend to cut it down
raises it a handbreadth from the ground and cuts.
With a thick sycamore: two handbreadths.
With an untouched sycamore: three handbreadths.
With reeds and grapevines —
from the knot and upward.
With palms and cedars —
he digs down and uproots,
because its trunk does not grow back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 1 that a cedar regrows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a cedar's trunk grows back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lets a buyer uproot cedars because they never regrow, which contradicts step 1.

steps.title: Answer: there are different kinds of cedar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources are talking about different kinds of cedar, following רבה בר הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With other kinds of cedar, as רבה בר הונא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash. 'Cedar' covers several kinds of tree, and they do not all behave the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction. One source is talking about a kind of cedar that regrows, and the other about a kind that does not. The idea that there are many kinds of cedar comes from רבה בר הונא, quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With other kinds of cedars,
in line with Rabba bar Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן בִּשְׁאָר מִינֵי אֲרָזִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: different kinds of cedar behave differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All cedars are one type, so the ברייתא and the פסוק contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are several kinds of cedar. Some regrow and some do not, so both sources are true.

steps.title: Source: ten kinds of cedar
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא says there are ten kinds of cedar and brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה בר הונא said: there are ten kinds of cedar, as it says, 'I will place in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבה בר הונא's statement to back up the answer in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר הונא says there are ten kinds of cedar. He brings this פסוק, which names cedar together with several other trees, as support. This shows that 'cedar' is a whole group of trees, which is what lets step 4 say that one kind regrows and another does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge is answered: 'cedar' is a family of ten kinds, so the פסוק and the ברייתא can each be talking about a different kind.

phrases.english: For Rabba bar Huna said:
There are ten kinds of cedars,
as it says:
"I will place in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That 'cedar' includes more than one kind of tree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר הונא, based on ישעיהו 41:19.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's thirteen fasts bring no rain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי אליעזר decreed thirteen fasts with no rain. After the last fast, the people started to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: there was an incident with רבי אליעזר, who decreed thirteen fasts on the community, and rain did not fall. At the last one, the people began to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: a story about fasting for rain. This step sets the scene for what רבי אליעזר does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thirteen fasts is the full set of fasts for a drought, and still no rain came. The people seemed ready to give up and go home. That sets up the turning point in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident; a story that happened

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁגָּזַר שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: who decreed thirteen fasts on the community
and rain did not fall.
At the last one, the community began to leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, not connected to the cedar discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after the full thirteen fasts, rain did not come for רבי אליעזר's community.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's sharp words move the people to tears, and rain falls
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks the people if they have prepared graves for themselves. They all burst into tears, and rain falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Have you prepared graves for yourselves?!' All the people burst out crying, and rain fell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר shakes the people up with a sharp question. Their heartfelt crying finally brings the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question warns that without rain there will be hunger and death, so walking away is like getting ready to die. The thirteen fasts did not bring rain, but the people's real crying did.
steps.whatToRemember: In this story, what finally brought the rain was the people's heartfelt crying after רבי אליעזר shook them up.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Have you prepared graves for yourselves?!
All the people burst out crying,
and rain fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes the story begun in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people's heartfelt crying, stirred by רבי אליעזר's words, brought the rain.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's short prayer brings rain
steps.stepSummary: A second story: רבי אליעזר leads the prayers with twenty-four blessings and is not answered. רבי עקיבא then says a short prayer, אבינו מלכנו, and rain falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another story about רבי אליעזר: he went down to lead the prayers before the ark and said twenty-four blessings, but he was not answered. רבי עקיבא went down after him and said: 'Our Father, our King, we have no king but You. Our Father, our King, for Your sake have mercy on us.' And rain fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about רבי אליעזר praying for rain. This time his student רבי עקיבא is answered right away, but his teacher was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said the full, long fast-day prayer and nothing happened. רבי עקיבא said only a few short words and rain came at once. This sets up a puzzle, because it looks as if the student was greater than the teacher. The next step solves it.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before the ark, meaning he led the prayers
Twenty-four blessings, the long prayer said on a public fast day

phrases.english: Another story about Rabbi Eliezer
who went down before the ark,
phrases.notes: He led the congregation in prayer on a fast day.

phrases.english: and he said twenty-four blessings
and he was not answered.
Rabbi Akiva went down after him and said:

phrases.aramaic: ״אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אָתָּה.
phrases.english: "Our Father, our King, we have no king but You.
Our Father, our King, for Your sake have mercy on us,"
and rain fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about רבי אליעזר and a fast for rain, following the story in steps 6-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's short prayer was answered with rain, while רבי אליעזר's long prayer was not.

steps.title: A heavenly voice explains why רבי עקיבא was answered
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis whisper about the story. A בת קול says רבי עקיבא is not greater than רבי אליעזר. He was answered because he lets go of hurts done to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis were whispering about it. A heavenly voice came out and said: It is not because this one is greater than that one. It is because this one lets go of what others do to him, and that one does not let go.
steps.whatsHappening: The Rabbis are puzzled that the student was answered and the teacher was not. A בת קול explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis may have thought this showed רבי עקיבא was the greater person. The בת קול says no. The difference is in character: רבי עקיבא forgives and lets things go, so Heaven treated him the same way and forgave too.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets go of hurts done to him; forgiving

steps.whatToRemember: Being answered in prayer here does not show who is greater. It comes from a forgiving nature: someone who lets things go is treated the same way by Heaven.
steps.confusionAlert: The בת קול does not say רבי אליעזר was a lesser person. It says outright that greatness is not the reason.

phrases.english: The Rabbis were whispering,
a heavenly voice came out and said:
Not because this one is greater than that one,
but because this one lets go of what is done to him,
and that one does not let go of what is done to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲווֹ מְרַנְּנִי רַבָּנַן, יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the puzzle raised by the story in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא was answered because he is forgiving, not because he was greater than רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: How much rain is needed to stop fasting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how deep the rain must soak before the community stops fasting. רבי מאיר says the depth of a plow blade. The חכמים give a measure that depends on the kind of soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How much rain must fall for the community to stop their fasts? Enough to soak as deep as a plow blade, up to where it bends. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: in dry ground, one handbreadth; in average ground, two handbreadths; in plowed ground, three handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new topic: the measure of rain that lets a community stop its fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives one measure for all ground: the depth of a plow blade. The חכמים say it depends on the soil. Dry ground needs one טפח, average ground needs two, and soft plowed ground needs three, since water sinks into it easily.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
The bend of the plow; the depth of the plow blade

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How much must the rain fall
for the community to stop their fasts?
As deep as the full plow blade, up to its bend,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
In dry ground, one handbreadth;
in average ground, two handbreadths;
in plowed ground, three handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד מָתַי יְהוּ הַגְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories of fasting for rain, the גמרא turns to the practical rule of when such a fast ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: rain soaking to the depth of a plow blade. חכמים: one טפח in dry ground, two in average ground, three in plowed ground.

steps.title: The deep rises three handbreadths to meet the rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that for every טפח of rain that soaks down, water from the deep rises three טפחים to meet it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: There is no handbreadth of rain from above that the deep does not rise three handbreadths to meet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about water from below rising up to meet the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds new information to the measures in step 10. Rain does not only soak down from above. Water from the deep also rises from below, three times as much. This statement sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The deep; the waters under the earth

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
There is no handbreadth of rain from above

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין תְּהוֹם יוֹצֵא לִקְרָאתוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.english: that the deep does not rise three handbreadths to meet.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of rain soaking into the ground by adding water rising from below.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For each טפח of rain from above, the deep rises three טפחים.

steps.title: Another teaching says only two handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: another ברייתא says the deep rises only two טפחים, not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in another ברייתא that it rises two handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said three טפחים, but another teaching says two. Both cannot be right about the same case, so the גמרא asks how they fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught; this opens a contradiction from another ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught: two handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number in step 11 using a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that the deep rises three טפחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the deep rises only two טפחים, which contradicts three.

steps.title: Plowed ground versus unplowed ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two teachings speak about different ground: three טפחים in plowed ground, two in unplowed ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is speaking about plowed ground, and there it is speaking about ground that is not plowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא speaks about a different kind of ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water moves more easily through soft, plowed soil, so there the deep rises three טפחים. In hard, unplowed ground it rises only two. The two teachings do not argue; they describe two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources can both be true
Here... there; each source speaks of a different case

steps.whatToRemember: How high the deep rises depends on the soil: three טפחים in plowed ground, two in unplowed ground.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it speaks of plowed ground;
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's three טפחים.

phrases.english: there, it speaks of ground that is not plowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בַּעֲבוּדָה, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ עֲבוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks about a different type of ground.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if the two ברייתות disagree about how high the deep rises.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three טפחים applies to plowed ground and two טפחים to unplowed ground, so there is no argument.

steps.title: The deep waters call to each other at the water pouring
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that when water is poured on the altar on סוכות, one deep tells the other to let its waters flow, because it hears the sound of two friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: When they pour the water on the altar on the festival, one deep says to its fellow: Let your waters flow, I hear the sound of two friends.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a new teaching about the deep: it responds to the water pouring on the altar on סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the deep rising toward the waters above. On סוכות both water and wine are poured on the altar. These are the 'two friends'. When the deep hears them, it calls to the other deep to let its waters flow.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring the water on the altar, the water libation of סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
When they pour the water on the altar on the festival,
one deep says to its fellow:
Let your waters flow,
I hear the sound of two friends.
phrases.notes: The two friends are the water and the wine poured on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כְּשֶׁמְּנַסְּכִין אֶת הַמַּיִם בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the deep waters responding to the waters above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When water is poured on the altar on סוכות, the deep waters call to each other to flow.

steps.title: The verse: deep calls to deep
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר supports his teaching with a פסוק from תהלים: 'Deep calls to deep at the sound of Your channels.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Deep calls to deep at the sound of Your channels, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק as the source for what he just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'deep calls to deep' as one deep calling to the other. He reads 'the sound of Your channels' as the sound of the liquids poured down the altar's channels. So the פסוק fits his teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says; this brings a פסוק as a source

steps.whatToRemember: The deep waters below respond to what is done above, both to rain and to the pouring of water on the altar on סוכות.

phrases.english: As it says:
"Deep calls to deep
at the sound of Your channels, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אלעזר's statement in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the deep waters call to each other when the water is poured on the altar on סוכות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 42:8: 'Deep calls to deep at the sound of Your channels.'

steps.title: רבה describes the angel רידיא who controls the waters
steps.stepSummary: רבה says he saw רידיא, a calf-like figure standing between the upper and lower deep. It tells the upper waters to rain down and the lower waters to rise up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I myself saw רידיא. It looks like a calf with parted lips and stands between the lower deep and the upper deep. To the upper deep it says, 'Let your waters drip down.' To the lower deep it says, 'Let your waters flow up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a personal report about the angel in charge of water, continuing the theme of the upper and lower waters meeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 14 taught that the deep waters rise in response to the waters above: the rain in step 11 and the water libation in step 14. רבה now names who directs this. One figure gives both commands: rain comes down from above and water rises from below.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of the angel in charge of the waters
The lower deep (waters under the earth)
The upper deep (waters above, the source of rain)
Let drip down, release as rain

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I myself saw this Ridya,
phrases.notes: רידיא is the angel in charge of the waters.

phrases.english: it looks like a calf, and its lips are parted,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָיְימָא בֵּין תְּהוֹמָא תַּתָּאָה לִתְהוֹמָא עִילָּאָה.
phrases.english: and it stands between the lower deep and the upper deep.
To the upper deep it says:
Let your waters drip down.
To the lower deep it says:
Let your waters flow up,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי הַאי רִידְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadic theme of the upper and lower waters meeting from steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel רידיא stands between the upper and lower deep and commands the upper waters to rain and the lower waters to rise.

steps.title: A verse from שיר השירים supports רבה
steps.stepSummary: רבה supports his description with the פסוק 'The blossoms appear on the earth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The blossoms appear on the earth, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a פסוק to back up what he described about רידיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as a hint to רידיא and the rising waters. The hint comes from the rest of the verse, which the גמרא leaves out under 'וגו׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"The blossoms appear on the earth, etc."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:12. The verse goes on 'וקול התור', and תור can also mean an ox, a hint to the calf-like רידיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural support for רבה's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's description of רידיא and the waters

steps.title: When rain falls during a fast: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says rain before sunrise ends the fast, but rain after sunrise means they finish it. רבי יהודה moves the cutoff to midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If they were fasting and rain fell before sunrise, etc. The Rabbis taught: If they were fasting and rain fell before sunrise, they do not finish the fast. If it fell after sunrise, they finish it. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: before midday they do not finish; after midday they finish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives different cutoff times for when a fast for rain must still be completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is: if the rain they fasted for arrives, can they stop fasting? Both opinions agree that early rain ends the fast and late rain does not. They only disagree on the cutoff: sunrise for רבי מאיר, midday for רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'They complete' does not mean the rain didn't count. It means the fast had already taken hold, so they finish it even though the rain came.

phrases.english: If they were fasting and rain fell
before sunrise, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
If they were fasting and rain fell for them,
before sunrise, they do not complete the fast.
After sunrise, they complete it,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Before midday, they do not complete it.
After midday, they complete it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין וְיָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים קוֹדֶם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא leaves the אגדה about the waters and returns to the משנה's הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי מאיר, rain after sunrise means the fast is completed. Per רבי יהודה, the cutoff is midday.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view: the ninth hour
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי puts the cutoff even later, at the ninth hour of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Before the ninth hour they do not finish the fast. After the ninth hour they finish it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the same ברייתא gives the latest cutoff of all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion pushes the cutoff later: sunrise, then midday, then the ninth hour. Under רבי יוסי, rain that comes even in the early afternoon still lets them stop fasting.

keyTerms.meaning: The ninth hour of the day, about three hours after midday

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Before the ninth hour, they do not complete the fast,
phrases.notes: The day is counted in twelve hours, so the ninth hour is about three hours after midday.

phrases.english: after the ninth hour, they complete it,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: קוֹדֶם תֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cutoff for completing the fast is the ninth hour.

steps.title: Proof from אחאב's fast
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves his view from אחאב, who fasted from the ninth hour onward and was still counted as having humbled himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we find that אחאב, king of Israel, fasted from the ninth hour onward, as it says: 'Do you see how אחאב has humbled himself, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a source to show why the ninth hour is the key time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב's fast started at the ninth hour, and the פסוק still treats it as a real fast. So the hours from the ninth hour onward can make up a fast, which is why רבי יוסי sets the cutoff there.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we find (introduces a precedent)

phrases.english: for so we find with Ahab, king of Israel,
that he fasted from the ninth hour and onward,
as it is stated: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוסי's ninth-hour cutoff.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 21:29, אחאב's fast from the ninth hour

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה plans to finish the fast
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה declared a fast. Rain fell after sunrise, and he planned to have the people finish the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה declared a fast, and rain fell after sunrise. He thought he should have them complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case to show which opinion we follow. This step sets up the next move, where רבי אמי responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain after sunrise is exactly where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree. רבי יהודה נשיאה's plan to finish the fast follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to have them complete it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia decreed a fast,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָרְדוּ לָהֶם גְּשָׁמִים לְאַחַר הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.english: and rain fell for them after sunrise.
He thought to have them complete the fast,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's dispute to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain fell after sunrise, and רבי יהודה נשיאה intended to have the fast completed, like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the cutoff is midday
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells him the rule is 'before midday and after midday,' so there is no need to finish the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: We learned 'before midday and after midday.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי rejects רבי יהודה נשיאה's plan and tells him the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the rain came before midday, under רבי יהודה's view the people do not need to finish the fast. This story settles the הלכה in favor of רבי יהודה over רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (we have a teaching that says)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: if rain falls before midday, the fast does not need to be completed. If it falls after midday, the fast is completed, following רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical הלכה among the three opinions in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
"Before midday and after midday" is what we learned.
phrases.notes: He means we follow רבי יהודה, so rain this early ends the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת וְאַחַר חֲצוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan in step 21 and establishes the halacha.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יהודה נשיאה's plan to have the fast completed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He followed רבי מאיר, but the halacha follows רבי יהודה's midday cutoff.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן's fast: rain before sunrise
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן declared a fast, and rain fell before sunrise. The people thought this showed how worthy the community was.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן declared a fast, and rain fell before sunrise. The people thought to say: This shows the praise of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second story about rain arriving early. This step sets up the next move, where שמואל הקטן will respond to the people's assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain came even before the fast began, and the people took it as a sign that they were especially worthy. The story is not finished here. The response to the people's view comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא known for his great humility

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan decreed a fast,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָרְדוּ לָהֶם גְּשָׁמִים קוֹדֶם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.english: and rain fell for them before sunrise.
The people thought to say:
It is the praise of the community.
phrases.notes: They felt they got rain without even needing to pray, so they must be very worthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, again about rain arriving early during a fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain fell before sunrise on שמואל הקטן's fast, and the people took it as a sign of their merit.

steps.title: The first parable: a master who gives just to stop hearing the servant
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן rejects the idea that early rain shows merit. He compares it to a master who quickly gives his servant what he asks so he will not have to hear him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will give you a parable. What is this like? Like a servant who asks his master for a gift. The master says: Give it to him, and let me not hear his voice.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל הקטן answers the people from the last step, who thought that rain before sunrise showed how worthy they were. He tells them it means the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people read fast rain as a reward for their merit. שמואל הקטן reads it as a sign that Heaven did not want to hear their prayers at all, so the answer came before they could even pray.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift or payment, here food or support
And let me not hear his voice

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל הקטן, answering the people who thought the early rain showed their merit.

phrases.english: I will give you a parable,
what is this matter like —
like a servant who asks his master for a gift,
he said to them: Give it to him,
phrases.notes: Here "he" is the master, speaking to his helpers.

phrases.english: and let me not hear his voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the people's reading of the early rain in step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The people's assumption that rain before sunrise shows the community's merit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A fast answer can mean Heaven does not want to hear the prayers, not that the people are worthy

steps.title: A second fast: rain comes after sunset
steps.stepSummary: On another occasion, שמואל הקטן declared a fast and the rain came only after sunset. The people again thought this showed their merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again, שמואל הקטן declared a fast, and rain fell after sunset. The people thought: this is a sign of the community's merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about שמואל הקטן. It sets up his next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he said that early rain is not a good sign, the people reasoned that late rain must be good. It would seem that Heaven listened to their prayers all day long.

keyTerms.meaning: The praise or merit of the community

phrases.english: Again, שמואל הקטן declared a fast
and rain fell for them
after sunset.
The people thought to say
it is the praise of the community,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel story to step 23, now with the rain coming late
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain fell after sunset on שמואל הקטן's fast, and the people took it as a sign of merit

steps.title: The second parable: a master who makes the servant suffer first
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן says late rain is also not a sign of merit. It is like a master who makes his servant wait and suffer before giving him anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to them: It is not the community's merit. Rather, I will give you a parable. What is this like? Like a servant who asks his master for a gift, and the master says: Wait until he wastes away and suffers, and only then give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל הקטן rejects the people's new idea. He gives a second parable to show that late rain is not a good sign either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Early rain meant Heaven did not want to hear them. Late rain means Heaven wanted them to suffer before helping. Either way, the timing alone does not show the community's merit.

keyTerms.meaning: That he wastes away, grows weak

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think early rain is bad and late rain is good. שמואל הקטן says neither one, by itself, proves the community's merit.

phrases.english: שמואל said to them:
It is not the praise of the community,
rather, I will give you a parable,
what is this matter like —
like a servant who asks his master for a gift,
and he said to them: Wait with him
until he wastes away and suffers,
and afterward give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שֶׁבַח שֶׁל צִבּוּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the people's reading of the late rain in step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that rain after sunset shows the community's merit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A delayed answer can mean Heaven wanted them to suffer first, not that they are worthy

steps.title: So what does count as merit for שמואל הקטן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if neither early nor late rain shows merit, what would show it according to שמואל הקטן?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל הקטן, what would the community's merit look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל הקטן rejected both early rain and late rain as signs of merit. That makes us wonder whether any timing would count as a sign of Heaven's approval.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: And according to שמואל הקטן,
what does the praise of the community look like?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל הַקָּטָן שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל צִבּוּר הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from his two rejections and asks what a true sign of merit would be
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of rainfall would show the community's merit according to שמואל הקטן

steps.title: Real merit: the wind and rain come at the very words of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when the prayer leader says "משיב הרוח" and the wind blows right away, and says "מוריד הגשם" and the rain comes right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said "Who makes the wind blow," and the wind blew. He said "Who makes the rain fall," and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. A true sign of merit is when Heaven answers at the exact moment of the prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Early rain means Heaven did not want to hear the prayer, and late rain means the people had to suffer first. Rain that comes right as they pray shows the prayer itself was wanted and answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Who makes the wind blow, words from the עמידה
Who makes the rain fall, words from the עמידה

steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל הקטן, rain that is too early or too late is not a sign of merit. The sign of merit is an answer at the very moment of the prayer.

phrases.english: He said "Who makes the wind blow"
phrases.notes: "He" is the prayer leader, saying these words in the עמידה.

phrases.english: and the wind blew,
he said "Who makes the rain fall"
and the rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Merit shows when the wind and rain come at the moment the prayer leader mentions them

steps.title: Back to the משנה: why not say הלל right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the fast in לוד. There, rain fell, and the people ate first and only then said הלל. The גמרא asks why they did not say הלל immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: There was a story where they declared a fast in לוד, and so on. Why not say הלל at the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its story about לוד. It asks why the people delayed saying הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the people went home, ate and drank, and only afterward came back to say הלל. It seems more fitting to praise ה׳ right away, at the moment of the miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: לוד, a city in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: There was an incident where they declared a fast in לוד, and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. There, rain fell, they went home to eat and drink, and then came back to say הלל.

phrases.english: So let them say הלל from the start?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל הקטן stories and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the people in לוד ate first and said הלל only afterward

steps.title: אביי and רבא begin their answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both begin to explain that הלל is not said in a certain situation. Their sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: Because one does not say הלל
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the answer to why הלל was delayed. The answer is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great אמוראים agree on one answer: there is some condition under which הלל is not said. That condition explains why the people of לוד first went home to eat.

phrases.english: אביי and רבא both said:
Because one does not say הלל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a condition under which הלל is not said, which is why they ate first; the full condition follows in the next part of the text
